newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--There was a temporary slide in the drachma in March against almost all currencies, according to the Federation of Exporters, which says that the basket of foreign currencies rose 0.5 percent against the drachma while European currencies rose 0.23 percent. If this trend continues, exporters say, the drachma will fall by 3.0 percent against foreign currencies and 1.1 percent against European currencies by the end of the year.

-- Labour Minister Miltaides Papaioannnou yesterday made clear his position on recent controversial statements by the prime minister on labour relations, saying the cost of labour was not the only factor to blame for lack of competitiveness in the Greek eocnomy.

--The Aspropyrgos Refineries last year posted their biggest ever profits while three state-run companies and two private refineries (DEP, Motor Oil and Petrola) had total sales of 920 billion drachmas.

--Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, needs a new reform programme for administration and operation, foreign consultants McKinsey have recommended, calling the programme "sharing the burden equally".

--Inflation has seen a significant drop this month, settling at close to 6.0 percent. Reliable sources say the consumer price index for March will close at around 6.1 percent, down from 6.6 in February.
--A percentage of 10.5-12 percent will be offered for OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation's, second share float. The final decisions will be made at today's Cabinet meeting.
--The state-run National Bank of Greece will issue a subordinated callable bond loan of up to $200 million with maturity up to 10 years in May or June.

--Seven retail firms will be brought to the courts on charges of irregularities in charging credit cards for sales of items. The development ministry in cooperation with the Association of Greek Banks is working on reforming the legislative framework governing credit cards.

--The course of tax revenues for the state continues to be disappointing with the latest reports saying that the rate of increase for revenues in March was below 10.0 percent, and below the forecast annual rate of 14.6 percent.

--The prime minister has made a personal intervention with the administration of the Panhellenic Seamen's Federation to find realistic solutions to problems and help stop vessels abandoning the Greek shipping register.

--The disappointing performance of financial inflows in the first three months of the state has created serious problems if the government is to meet budget targets this year. A meeting chaired by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou yesterday examined alternatives.
--May will see the beginning of an information campaign to brief Greeks on the Community Support Framework, budgeted at three billion drachmas.

--A wave of strikes is on the horizon as banks and workers in public utilities and organisations (DEKOs) buck against the government's insistence on fiscal discipline. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
